questions.q: What does this lesson identify as the real migration path into Azure SQL Database, instead of native T-SQL RESTORE?
options: Exporting to a BACPAC and importing it (via az sql db import), or using Database Migration Service for larger/online moves
Running RESTORE DATABASE ... FROM URL directly, exactly as on Managed Instance
Manually copying .mdf and .ldf files into Azure Blob Storage
There is no supported migration path into Azure SQL Database at all
questions.explain: Azure SQL Database does not support native RESTORE FROM URL — BACPAC import and DMS are the real, documented paths.

questions.q: Why doesn't RESTORE DATABASE ... FROM URL work as a migration path into Azure SQL Database, per this lesson?
options: Because that native T-SQL restore capability belongs to Managed Instance and SQL Server on Azure VM, not the singleton Azure SQL Database
Because URL-based restores were permanently removed from all of Azure SQL
Because Azure SQL Database only accepts restores from local disk
Because RESTORE DATABASE is deprecated T-SQL syntax everywhere
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that this is a fact that trips up DBAs coming from on-prem — it's a Managed Instance/VM capability, not an Azure SQL Database one.

questions.q: Which three feature parity gaps does this lesson name as specific to Azure SQL Database as a migration target?
options: No cross-database queries/three-part names, no full SQL Server Agent scheduler, and no linked servers
No support for stored procedures, no support for indexes, no support for views
No support for encryption of any kind
No support for the T-SQL SELECT statement
questions.explain: These specific gaps stem from Azure SQL Database being a single isolated database rather than a full instance.

questions.q: What is a BACPAC, as described in this lesson?
options: A portable package containing schema and data, exported from a source database and imported into a new Azure SQL Database
A native binary backup file usable only with RESTORE DATABASE
A type of Azure virtual network configuration
A PowerShell module for managing Elastic Jobs
questions.explain: az sql db import consumes a BACPAC file to bring schema and data into a new Azure SQL Database.

questions.q: When does this lesson say Database Migration Service (DMS) is the better fit over a BACPAC export/import?
options: For a large database, or when the online migration strategy from the previous lesson is the right call
Only for databases smaller than 1 MB
Only when there is no source database at all
DMS and BACPAC import are functionally identical in every scenario with no trade-offs
questions.explain: DMS handles continuous sync with a short cutover, which fits the online-migration case and large databases better than a single offline export/import.
